science.title: The Brain Predicts Social Interaction Before It Starts New Study Finds
science.description: New neuroscience study on how the brain generates social behavior. Using whole-brain imaging during live social interactions in zebrafish, researchers found that the brain enters a distinct neural state several seconds before an animal approaches another individual. The signal predicts not only whether an upcoming action will be social, but also how social the individual is overall. The team also identified neurons in the pallium that appear to promote social approach behavior, linking a specific neural population to social drive. The work offers a rare brain-wide view of how social decisions are formed, provide insight into why individuals differ in sociability , and open a window into the neural mechanisms underlying social deficits.

science.title: Infrastructure and policy reforms to facilitate collaboration in medical research
science.description: Medical research increasingly depends on data-driven, large-scale, multicentric cooperation; however, such cooperation remains obstructed by fragmented procedures, heterogeneity in ethics oversight, complex legal frameworks and regulatory divergence. These structural barriers slow progress, increase costs and ultimately limit benefits to patients. Harmonized, efficient processes and coherent legal frameworks that enable effective collaborative research are feasible and urgently needed.
